questions.markdown:
Consider a Markov chain with the following transition probability matrix

$$
P=\begin{bmatrix}
0.6 & 0.2 & 0.2\\
0.3 & 0.5 & 0.2\\
0.4 & 0.3 & 0.3
\end{bmatrix}
$$

Determine $P[X_5=2\mid X_2=0]$.
Classify the states into recurrent and transient states along with their periodicity for the above state transition diagram.

questions.markdown:
Consider the Markov chain with three states, $S=\{1,2,3\}$ that has the following transition probability matrix

$$
P=\begin{bmatrix}
1/2 & 1/4 & 1/4\\
1/3 & 0 & 2/3\\
1/2 & 1/2 & 0
\end{bmatrix}
$$

If we know $P(X_1=1)=P(X_1=2)=1/4$, find $P\,(X_1=3,\,X_2=2,\,X_3=1)$.

questions.markdown:
For sufficiently small $h>0$, prove the following property of the Poisson process $\{X(t):t\geq 0\}$ with state space $S=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$,

$$
p_{i,i+1}(h)=P\{X(t+h)=i+1\mid X(t)=i\}=\lambda h+o(h)
$$

where $o(h)$ is the order of $h$ and satisfies $\lim_{h\to 0}\dfrac{o(h)}{h}=0$, $\lambda$ is the rate of occurrence of events.

At steady state, prove that

$$
p_0=\frac{1}{\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\rho^n}
$$

for M/M/1 queuing models where $\rho$ is utilisation factor and $p_0$ represents `0' number of customers or arrivals in the system at steady state.

A supermarket has two sales girls at the sales counters. The service time for each customer is exponential with a mean of 4 minutes, and the people arrive in a Poisson fashion at the rate of 10 an hour. If a customer has to wait, what is the expected length of his waiting time?

Let $X=\{X_1,X_2\}$ and $Y=\{Y_1,Y_2\}$ be two groups of variables and $Z=(X,\,Y)^T$. The covariance matrix of $Z$ is given below.

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
5.0 & 1.5 & 0.8 & 2.2\\
1.5 & 4.3 & 1.0 & 1.8\\
0.8 & 1.0 & 3.7 & 0.6\\
2.2 & 1.8 & 0.6 & 6.0
\end{bmatrix}
$$

a. Find the Covariance of $(X_1,Y_1)$.

b. Find the Variance of $Y_2$.

The data matrix for a random sample of size $N=3$ from a bivariate normal population is given by

$$
X=\begin{pmatrix}
4 & 7\\
8 & 6\\
12 & 8
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Evaluate the observed $T^2$ statistic for

$$
\mu_0=\begin{pmatrix}10\\7\end{pmatrix}
$$

and covariance matrix

$$
S=\begin{pmatrix}
16 & 2\\
2 & 1
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

A regression analysis involves 40 observations and five independent variables, $\mathrm{SSE}=93.5$ and $\mathrm{SST}=150.3$

a. Compute the $F$ statistic

b. Compute the coefficient of determination

c. Compute the Adjusted $R^2$

d. Compute the standard error of the estimate

e. Conduct an $F$-test at $\alpha=.05$ for the overall significance of the relationship.

If there are two variables (or datasets) it indicates that the covariance matrix will be 2 dimensional. Suppose the math and science scores of 3 students are given as follows:

| Student | Math (X) | Science (Y) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 92 | 80 |
| 2 | 60 | 30 |
| 3 | 100 | 70 |

Calculate the covariance matrix for the above data.

questions.markdown:
In a one-way MANOVA involving 3 groups and 2 response variables, the following matrices are given:

- Between-group sum of squares and cross-products matrix $(B)$:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
25 & 5\\
5 & 20
\end{pmatrix}
$$

- Within-group sum of squares and cross-products matrix $(W)$:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
75 & 20\\
20 & 60
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Compute the Wilks' Lambda statistic $(\Lambda)$.

The following observations on two responses are collected for three treatments. The observation vectors $\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{bmatrix}$ are

Treatment 1: $\begin{bmatrix}6\\7\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}5\\9\end{bmatrix}$,

Treatment 2: $\begin{bmatrix}3\\3\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}1\\6\end{bmatrix}$,

Treatment 3: $\begin{bmatrix}2\\3\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix}5\\1\end{bmatrix}$.

Construct the one-way MANOVA Table.

questions.markdown:
Two independent random samples were drawn from two multivariate normal populations with two variables $X_1$ and $X_2$. The data from the two samples are as follows:

For group-1:

$$
\bar{X}=\begin{bmatrix}5.2\\3.8\end{bmatrix};\quad S=\begin{pmatrix}1.2 & 0.65\\0.65 & 0.9\end{pmatrix},\quad n_1=10
$$

For group-2:

$$
\bar{X}=\begin{bmatrix}4.6\\4.1\end{bmatrix};\quad S=\begin{pmatrix}1.8 & 0.85\\0.85 & 1.1\end{pmatrix},\quad n_2=12
$$

Test whether the mean vectors of the two samples are significantly different from each other at 5% significance level.
Consider a set of 7 one-dimensional data points, $1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 15, 16$. Apply Agglomerative clustering algorithm to build the dendogram. Merge the clusters using MIN distance.

Compute the liner discriminant projection of the following two-dimensional dataset:

- Class $C_1$: $(4,4)$, $(2,4)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,6)$
- Class $C_2$: $(10,8)$, $(6,8)$, $(9,5)$, $(8,7)$
